results.title: Blocking finding open against a *different version* of the same model blocks approval of this one
results.evidence: refused, naming the finding raised against 1.0.0

results.title: Close the blocking finding, then re-attempt the same conclusion
results.evidence: refused while open, approved once the finding closed

results.title: Record a result after the episode concluded
Open with `snapshot_id` naming a snapshot that does not exist
results.evidence: accepted at open and discovered only at replay ('validation_refused'): the episode carries a pin to 'snap-does-not-exist' for as long as nobody replays it, and the failure lands on whoever asked for the evidence rather than on whoever typed the identifier

results.title: Open an episode with no validators
Open with the same validator listed twice
results.evidence: one validator is recorded twice: ['person/validator', 'person/validator'] and the capacity view has them carrying 4 episodes. The capacity view appends the episode once per entry, so a duplicate inflates that person's open load

results.title: `due_at` set to a moment in the past at open
results.evidence: an episode opened a week overdue is stored with that date and read by nothing: the queue and the backlog both compute what falls due from the re-validation triggers, so `due_at` is written at open and never evaluated — a date somebody will believe is enforced
